digest.component_or_area: reconciler committed state cache and tickets repository
propositions: The tickets repository branch is 1.04 GiB due to 92% being the reconciler's .bridge_state cache, where baseline_advanced_at and last_get_pass fields represent bookkeeping writes that no code reads, causing poor git delta compression (12.79 KB marginal cost per version)

Deleting baseline_advanced_at and moving last_get_pass to a separate file reduces marginal packed cost to 1.74 KB per version (7.4x improvement) with the timestamp removal and 12.8x total improvement including rotation bookkeeping relocation

The .bridge_state cache must remain committed on-branch because the reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners, requiring durable state in git, but the cache content and churn (not location) are the optimization levers

A one-time history rewrite using git fast-export/fast-import reduces the existing 1.17 GB repository to 98.8 MB (8.4% of original) while preserving all 49,888 commits and 2,661 merges, with the rewritten HEAD tree byte-identical to pre-rewrite

Multiple committed-format changes (removing baseline_advanced_at, relocating last_get_pass, normalizing baseline fields, narrowing prev_snapshot.json) must maintain backward compatibility through mixed-version read paths and dual writes before legacy fields are removed

Rollout gates depend on observed descendant workflow execution, explicit host runtime refresh, live epoch-mismatch refusal probes, and a quiesced publication window with operator-attested zero active sessions and stopped rebar-mcp servers, eliminating fixed-delay requirements
